statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-56850 is a Node.js HTTPS Agent flaw: when a request passes pfx as an array of objects (each with buf and passphrase), https.Agent.getName() appends the array as text, so different client certificates give the same connection-pool key and a pooled TLS connection, with the mutual TLS client identity it was set up with, can be reused for a request configured with another certificate. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.23.2, the 2026-07-29 security release (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/july-2026-security-releases; release notes https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.2), and its CVE record lists 22.x as affected through 22.23.1. The 22.x fix is commit acaf4266b2, 'https: distinguish PFX object-array agent keys' (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/acaf4266b2), which carries this CVE id: it adds getPfxAgentKey() to lib/https.js, which builds the key from each entry's buffer and passphrase; in Node.js 22.23.1 getName() still appends options.pfx unchanged. We read usr/bin/node, the only file each package installs, in every nodejs-22 package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 2026-11-28, on x86_64 and aarch64: 13 builds from 22.22.0-r0 to the current 22.23.5-r0, each checked against its repository index checksum. 22.22.0-r0 through 22.23.1-r0 (22.22.0-r0, 22.22.1-r0, 22.22.2-r0, 22.22.2-r1, 22.22.3-r0, 22.23.0-r0 and 22.23.1-r0) report Node.js v22.22.0 through v22.23.1; 22.23.2-r0 is the first that reports v22.23.2, and 22.23.3-r0 through 22.23.5-r0 report v22.23.3 through v22.23.5. The lib/https.js source embedded in the binary contains getPfxAgentKey() and calls it from getName() in 22.23.2-r0 through 22.23.4-r2, and in none of the builds before 22.23.2-r0, which still append options.pfx directly. In 22.23.5-r0 getName() calls getKeyMaterialAgentKey() instead, which commit af6fbb6564 for CVE-2026-123877 (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/af6fbb6564) put in place of getPfxAgentKey(); it still builds the key from each pfx entry's buffer and passphrase, and that build does not append options.pfx directly either.
